item.title: Evaluating AI agents: moving past the vibe check
item.description: A practical engineering guide and reference architecture for establishing continuous evaluation pipelines for multi-turn AI agents using Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, Google ADK, and OpenInference standards.

item.title: Three layers, one repo: a tour of google/adk-recipes
item.description: The google/adk-recipes repository unifies Agent Development Kit (ADK) resources into three structured layers—core/, plugins/, and contrib/—serving as a single source of truth for building AI agents Developers can leverage reference patterns, install modular vertical skills (such as retail product search and virtual try-on) directly into their coding assistants, and deploy production-ready services across multiple languages This cohesive structure streamlines the entire workflow from initial scaffolding to full deployment on Google Cloud infrastructure.

item.title: Announcing DPoP Support for Google OAuth: Securing Refresh Tokens
item.description: Google OAuth Platform now supports DPoP (Demonstrating Proof-of-Possession) to sender-constrain refresh tokens, neutralizing Infostealer malware and adversary-in-the-middle attacks By cryptographically binding long-lived refresh tokens while maintaining short-lived access tokens as standard Bearer tokens, developers achieve robust credential security without incurring high-QPS API performance overhead Additionally, developers integrating multi-agent or Model Context Protocol (MCP) workloads can use Google Cloud Secure Token Service (STS) to handle secure token delegation across agent chains.

item.title: Continuous accountability for Verified bots
item.description: Identity alone doesn't guarantee a bot will behave responsibly We are introducing a system to continuously evaluate whether Verified bots honor site preferences, like robots.txt and HTTP 429s, ensuring they remain accountable over time.

item.title: Sync real-time Stripe data to Postgres with Stripe Data Pipeline
item.description: Applications rely on current Stripe data to fulfill orders, update customer accounts, and manage access to paid features Until now, developers have had to build and maintain custom integrations to keep application databases in sync with Stripe We’re introducing real-time sync to Postgres for Stripe Data Pipeline, which lets them keep databases current without having to build custom integrations.

item.title: TimeSeries Tiered Storage Journey: Kafka/Flink Streams to Native Cassandra Cold Reads
item.description: The users still use the same query interface:TimeSeries Tiered Storage Read PathThe Cold Tier Data Plane uses compaction metadata for aggressive planning and pruning, which dramatically reduces the S3 query fan-out The idea for tiering is simple:Read directly from these S3 backups instead of paying a separate data transfer cost to S3.Once TimeSeries marks a hot Time Slice as ready for cold storage, we can customize Cassandra to read directly from its backups, allowing us to delete the on-disk data copy As of Cassandra 4.1, we can leverage pluggable Memtables to redirect reads from “cold” tables directly to the backup storage in S3.-- create table for a given Time SliceCREATE TABLE data_20260616_00_04 ( ... ..., PRIMARY KEY ((time_series_id, time_bucket, event_bucket), event_time, event_id, key)) WITH CLUSTERING ORDER BY (event_time DESC, event_id DESC, key DESC)

item.title: Behind the Scenes: Evolving Netflix’s Ads Event Pipeline for Live — Part II
item.description: The heart of the job: we match each client event to the ad-serving response for the same impression, enriching it with the full serving context using a KeyedCoProcessFunctionDeduplicate We extract measurement beacons for our partners and route the enriched ad event to its downstream consumers.The ad server logs responses to Kafka rather than writing to a registry; the Flink job joins responses with client events in real time and routes enriched ad events downstream.The join is the interesting part We encode the serving region into the ad token, so when a client event arrives in the wrong region, we forward it to the region that owns its response

item.title: Netflix Conductor: The Next Chapter
item.description: You stand it up, keep it running, and scale it, even for work that’s bursty or runs rarely.So Conductor added managed tasks: built-in task types where Conductor drives the compute directly, with no long-lived worker for you to host or scale Stratum is the serverless function layer of Netflix’s Cosmos platform, purpose-built for media-processing workloads, and a Conductor STRATUM task is the natural way to call one from a workflow That’s a polling problem, and at scale it has its own failure mode, one that showed up most sharply for Studio Orchestrator, the heavy Conductor user behind the Media Production Suite pipelines from earlier in this post.Conductor clients poll for work using worker threads, and historically the number of threads was fixed per task type
